title: David McKinney:
headline: The WestEd researcher says it plainly: in 12 to 14 days of NBA Math Hoops, kids moved from the 50th to the 58th percentile in math.
story: David McKinney is a Senior Research Associate at WestEd. He ran the NBA Math Hoops study with Learn Fresh. This cut is the proof, in his plain words.

Why believe it: an RCT is the gold standard, because it rules out the teacher, the district, even what kids had for breakfast. Why schools care: they only buy proof, and this program is low cost with two hours of teacher training.

Loops: L1 “How much did the kids improve?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:14 (“58th percentile”). L2 “Why would a school say yes?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the button. Stakes: schools don't spend on things without impact.
do: Open mid-sentence on “if a student started the summer at the 50th percentile”, with the hook text already on screen.
Number cards when he says them: 50th → 58th percentile, 12 to 14 days, 2 hours of training.
Show kids playing (NYC B-roll) on the days line and the training line.
Super: David McKinney / Senior Research Associate, WestEd.
End right after “program”, then the end card: Read the full study.
dont: Do not criticise ed-tech or AI. Do not use part 2 04:28 to 04:52 or 05:42 “instead of how can computers solve all of our problems”.
Do not use the social-emotional results (part 2 00:50 to 02:23).
Do not say the result is true for other Learn Fresh programs. NBA Math Hoops only, and it is a supplement to math class, not a replacement.
Do not use his self-intro (00:15 to 01:22, three restarts).
No logo, name or fade at 0:00. No school names on screen.
